SUMMARY AND KEY POINTS:

  • Audi is the first automaker to jointly develop an LLM-powered Mobile Work Agent experience with Cerence AI
  • Available through the “connected work” app in the Audi Application Store, Mobile Work Agent addresses a longstanding industry challenge by bringing secure, voice-first access to Microsoft 365 into the vehicle with built-in enterprise security, governance, and identity awareness.
  • Audi drivers can use Microsoft Teams and Outlook to check email, review schedules, and join meetings through an experience designed specifically for the car.
  • The experience is available across 28 countries in the Audi A5, Audi Q5, Audi A6, Audi A6 e-tron, Audi Q7, and Audi Q9 from model year 2026 onwards.

BURLINGTON, Mass. and INGOLSTADT, Germany, Nov. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Cerence Inc. (NASDAQ: CRNC) (“Cerence AI”), a global AI company building trusted solutions for complex real-world environments, today announced that Audi is the first automaker to jointly develop an LLM-powered Mobile Work Agent experience with Cerence AI, in collaboration with Microsoft. The Audi A5, Audi Q5, Audi A6, Audi A6 e-tron, Audi Q7, and Audi Q9 from model year 2026 onwards now have secure, voice-first access to Microsoft 365 directly in the vehicle for the first time. Mobile Work Agent, available via the Audi Application Store as the “connected work” app, turns Audi vehicles into secure work environments, addressing a longstanding industry challenge: bringing workplace productivity tools into the vehicle without compromising security, governance, or the driving experience.

As demand grows for more flexible and connected ways to work, Mobile Work Agent brings enterprise-grade workplace experiences into the vehicle. By extending the Microsoft 365 platform with generative AI capabilities into Audi vehicles, Cerence AI and Audi, in collaboration with Microsoft, have created a safer, more secure, and more intuitive way for drivers to stay informed and manage tasks from the road. The Mobile Work Agent enables Audi drivers to access Microsoft Teams and Outlook through a voice-first experience designed specifically for use in the car. Drivers can check email, review schedules, and join meetings all while keeping their hands on the wheel and eyes on the road.

Historically, enterprise security and governance requirements have been a major barrier to extending workplace productivity tools beyond traditional endpoints. Mobile Work Agent addresses those requirements by integrating directly with Microsoft's security, identity, and compliance ecosystem. Mobile Work Agent is built on Microsoft Foundry, which provides agent-level governance and safety controls. It also integrates with Microsoft’s security, identity, and compliance ecosystem – including Intune, Entra, and Purview – to turn eligible Audi vehicles into trusted devices with secure, compliant access to the Microsoft 365 suite of productivity applications. It is GDPR and EU AI Act compliant.

“For years, the automotive and enterprise technology industries have recognized the opportunity to bring workplace experiences into the vehicle, but security, governance, and user experience requirements made that difficult to achieve at production scale,” said Nils Schanz, EVP, Product & Technology at Cerence AI. “With Audi and Microsoft, we've created a breakthrough solution, combining conversational AI, deep vehicle integration, and enterprise-grade trust to turn the vehicle into a secure extension of the workplace. Mobile Work Agent establishes a new foundation for how people interact with enterprise systems on the move and aligns with how people actually want to work: more safely, hands-free, and with full confidence that their data is protected.”

“Time on the road is valuable. Together with Cerence AI and Microsoft, we have developed an intelligent software solution that lets our customers make productive use of their time in the car," said Poorab Sarmah, Head of Occupant Interaction/Infotainment System Development, AUDI AG.

“AI delivers the most value when it meets people where they work, including on the road,” said Dayan Rodriguez, Corporate Vice President, Manufacturing and Mobility, Microsoft. “Audi's launch shows how enterprise trust and voice-first design can make the vehicle a secure extension of the workplace while delivering a similar experience to Microsoft Copilot on a PC or smartphone.”

To learn more about Cerence AI’s Mobile Work Agent, see here. For more information about Cerence AI, visit www.cerence.ai, and follow the company on LinkedIn.

Real estate technology company PropStream examines how integrated property data, AI-assisted analysis, and direct outreach are changing the way professionals identify opportunities and respond to homeowners.

LOS ANGELES, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- PropStream will be featured in an upcoming segment of "All Access hosted by Andy Garcia," a short-form documentary series distributed to Public Television stations nationwide. Filmed July 8, 2026, the feature explores the rise of the modern real estate entrepreneur and how AI and technology are used to search for properties, evaluate potential deals, connect with owners, and transact, all from one system.

Real estate has become a data-heavy business, but more information does not always produce clearer decisions. Property records, comparable sales, ownership details, market activity, and marketing tools are often spread across separate platforms. PropStream brings those functions together, allowing investors, agents, lenders, wholesalers, and other professionals to research on- and off-market properties, examine local trends, and identify properties whose circumstances may create a need for timely guidance.

"For 20 years, PropStream pioneered providing real estate professionals with nationwide public record data access, when information was spread across multiple sources. Today, the challenge has been turning that data into actionable opportunity," said Brian Tepfer, President of PropStream. "We're reinventing that experience from simply searching for data to communicating with data. With PropStream Intelligence AI, professionals can tell PropStream what opportunities they're looking for and quickly understand the properties and context behind the data. This new workflow allows them to quickly move from identifying an opportunity to connecting with an owner and closing a transaction, all within one platform. We're proud to have Andy Garcia and the All Access team showcase this evolution and the entrepreneurs who are using technology to build what comes next in real estate."

A homeowner may be preparing to relocate, downsize, renovate, refinance, or sell. PropStream's position is that better information can help real estate professionals approach owners with more relevant options, creating potential value for both the entrepreneur and the homeowner.

PropStream began approximately twenty years ago as a CD-ROM product that aggregated property information for investors. The platform has since expanded to include nationwide property searches, comparable-market analysis, investment calculators, owner contact information through third-party skip tracing providers, and outreach tools. What began as a way to collect scattered records has developed into a system that supports the process from the initial search through homeowner connection.

Artificial intelligence adds another layer without replacing professional judgment. PropStream's AI-supported tools help users interpret property information, perform rental comparisons, and navigate extensive datasets more efficiently. In a market shaped by fluctuating rates, limited inventory, and changing listing information, the company sees technology as a way to reduce fragmentation and help professionals make faster, better-informed decisions.

About "All Access hosted by Andy Garcia": "All Access hosted by Andy Garcia" presents short-form educational documentaries for Public Television audiences nationwide. The series explores the ideas, technologies, and organizations influencing contemporary life, using accessible storytelling to explain how industries are evolving and why those changes matter beyond the professionals working within them. The host introduces the series but does not conduct interviews with the organizations featured. More information is available at allaccessptv.com.

About PropStream: PropStream, a Stewart company, is a premier all-in-one real estate platform that empowers real estate professionals with unmatched aggregated data quality, accuracy, marketing tools, and a dialer. Founded in 2006, PropStream provides insights for over 160 million properties nationwide, leveraging PropStream Intelligence, predictive real estate records, and proprietary AI-driven analytics to support advanced filtering, featuring over 165 filters and 20 pre-built Lead Lists. PropStream helps real estate professionals identify the best off-market opportunities, comps, and connect with sellers more efficiently. PropStream was acquired by Stewart Information Services Corporation Technology Holdings (NYSE: STC) in November 2021 and has been named a HousingWire Tech 100 Honoree for six consecutive years since 2021.

LOS ANGELES, Nov. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem Inc. (NASDAQ: FFR) ("FFR" or the "Company"), a U.S.-based Embodied AI ("EAI") robotics company, today shared a weekly business update from YT Jia, Founder and Global CEO of FF and FFR.

"Welcome to my 82nd weekly report. Let me start with three major breakthroughs for FFR's education ecosystem in U.S. K–12 and career education. First, FFR is now an approved robotics supplier to a public school district that is considered top-tier both nationally and within California. We've cleared the district's review and joined its procurement platform. That means more than 1,000 schools in the district can now purchase FFR robots and our education productivity solutions directly. This week, the district's career education center led the way by purchasing several robots, including FX Navi and Aegis EDU. We hope the project will serve as a model for a broader rollout across the district.

Second, we signed a Strategic Education Partnership Framework Agreement with another public school district, one of California's leading districts. The district has also purchased robot devices including Master Mini and Aegis EDU. Third, we signed a Strategic Education Partnership Framework Agreement with an additional major public school district in Los Angeles.

The second and third partnerships both cover K–12 through adult education. We'll work with the two districts to develop curricula together, set up innovation labs, create career and technical education pathways, train teachers, and give students hands-on experience. Together, we'll explore how Physical AI education can connect what students learn in the classroom with further study, real-world practice, and career development. These two collaborations both renew automatically at the end of their terms. With these frameworks in place, we can move future projects forward quickly through a streamlined process.

Outside of California, we are also moving forward with strategic partnerships and sales in robotics education across multiple school districts in four other states: New York, Pennsylvania, Florida, and Texas. FFR pioneered K–12 robotics education in the U.S., and we're now No. 1 in the industry. The progress we've made on strategic partnerships and robot purchases across these three leading districts matters to FFR and to the whole industry. Let me share four reasons why:

First, it's a big step forward for our education ecosystem. By working with major school districts as strategic partners at the school district level, we can work directly with the U.S. public education system to build Physical AI education pathways that connect K–12 learning, technical skills training, and future careers.

Second, these projects give us a model for replicating at scale nationwide. The U.S. has more than 13,000 regular public-school districts. Across the country, about 130,000 public and private K–12 schools serve roughly 53 million students. That's a large market, with opportunities across robot devices, curricula, teacher training, and ongoing services. We'll learn from our first projects with leading districts, turn what works into a repeatable model, and gradually roll it out to across the country.

Third, it helps us move faster on our Four-Core Full-Stack AI business in education and speeds up the evolutionary flywheel. In real classrooms, we can deploy robot devices, develop Skills and solutions, and collect data in line with applicable requirements. That data helps us keep improving our Education Brain.

Fourth, it helps transform U.S. education in the Physical AI era. By making robots a regular part of teaching and hands-on learning, we can prepare the next generation of developers and skilled workers for the new era. As FFR's profile in the industry grows, we've received invitations from schools, universities, and school districts to take part in academic discussions and major exhibitions. I'll share more about those with you in future reports.

Regarding corporate governance, this week, we welcomed Carolyn Kissane to FFR's board as an independent director. Carolyn is the associate dean of New York University's Center for Global Affairs. She brings years of experience in higher education and knows how to bring universities, researchers, and companies together. Carolyn could help us grow our robotics education ecosystem, reach more developers, and build more industry partnerships. She'll also help us bring technology, talent, industry, and capital together. That will help us put our Four-Core Full-Stack AI strategy to work faster across all four industry ecosystems.

We also held our Middle East launch in Dubai this week. Six of our robots made their debut in the region. With our local partners, we showed five ways to put robots to work across our four industry ecosystems: education, security and inspection, entertainment, healthcare, and interactive sports. Together, we're opening a new chapter for Physical AI in the Middle East. We'll share a video from Dubai next week, so stay tuned.

For FFAI: it released its Q3 results this week. I want to highlight an important step we've taken on financial management and internal controls. After evaluating and testing the controls, FFAI management concluded that, as of September 30, 2026, FFAI had corrected all nine previously identified material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting. Management also concluded that the related controls were operating effectively. FFAI has spent nearly two years improving FFAI's financial management and internal controls. This progress puts us in a stronger position to meet our obligations as a public company, raise capital, and rebuild trust with investors. It also gives us a stronger foundation to grow and create value through our shared Robotaxi network, AI VisiCabin operations, and Physical AI investment and holdings business. All right, thanks for tuning in. I'll see you next week!"

FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem Inc. (NASDAQ: FFR) is a U.S.-based Embodied AI robotics company focused on the research and development, manufacturing, commercialization and deployment of intelligent robotic technologies, products and industry solutions. FFR is building a "Four-Core Full-Stack" AI ecosystem covering the full lifecycle of robotics, consisting of Physical AI Brain & Developer Platform, Physical AI Devices, Physical AI Industry Productivity Solutions, and Physical AI Data Factory. Guided by the technology and product philosophy of "One Brain, All Robots, Multi-capabilities," FFR aims to empower humanoid, biomimetic, and other robotic form factors through a unified Physical AI Brain, while continuously expanding their multi-task and multi-scenario capabilities. Smith+Nephew (LSE: SN, NYSE: SNN), the global medical technology business, announces Nick Alexos will join the company as Chief Financial Officer and the Board as an Executive Director on 30 November 2026. 

Nick brings more than 35 years of financial, commercial and transaction experience, with a strong track record of driving operational performance and creating value from complex situations across global businesses and private equity.

Nick was most recently Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer at Univar Solutions, a global distributor of chemicals and ingredients (2020-2026). He joined Univar Solutions when it was listed on the NYSE (UNVR) and played a central role in delivering the company’s operational transformation. In March 2023, Apollo Global announced it was acquiring Univar Solutions in an $8 billion take-private transaction, which resulted in the Company delisting in 2023. Subsequently Nick continued his work supporting the operational improvement of the business as Chief Financial Officer, and also had responsibility for Univar Solutions’ on-line service business.

Previously, Nick was Executive Vice President, Chief Financial Officer and Chief Administrative Officer of dental technology business Dentsply Sirona (2017-2019). As part of a new leadership team, he worked alongside the CEO to reshape the business to improve performance, including programmes focused on capital expenditure, inventory and cost control.

Prior to Dentsply Sirona, Nick spent 30 years at private equity firm Madison Dearborn Partners. As a Managing Director, he co-led 18 platform investments and was responsible for more than $14 billion of debt financings. His portfolio included multiple healthcare investments.

Rupert Soames, Chair of the Board, said: "Nick is an accomplished finance leader with deep experience across global businesses, public markets, private equity and capital markets. His track record in strategic transformation, M&A, financing and disciplined capital allocation will be highly valuable and we look forward to welcoming him to the Board."

Deepak Nath, Chief Executive Officer, said: "I am delighted to welcome Nick to Smith+Nephew. He brings strong financial and commercial leadership and has helped multiple businesses deliver significant value across his career. I look forward to working with him as we continue to sharpen execution, strengthen performance and deliver our strategic priorities."

Nick Alexos said: "I am excited to be joining Smith+Nephew, a global medical technology business with a strong heritage, leading positions in growing markets and significant potential. I look forward to working with Deepak, the Board and colleagues across the company to build on the progress already made and create sustainable value for our stakeholders."

Nick holds an MBA from the University of Chicago Booth School of Business and a BBA/CPA in Accounting / Finance from Loyola University, Chicago. He will be based in the United States, but is expected to travel widely.

“Welcome to my 82nd weekly report. Let me start with three major breakthroughs for FFR’s education ecosystem in U.S. K–12 and career education. First, FFR is now an approved robotics supplier to a public school district that is considered top-tier both nationally and within California. We’ve cleared the district’s review and joined its procurement platform. That means more than 1,000 schools in the district can now purchase FFR robots and our education productivity solutions directly. This week, the district’s career education center led the way by purchasing several robots, including FX Navi and Aegis EDU. We hope the project will serve as a model for a broader rollout across the district.

Second, we signed a Strategic Education Partnership Framework Agreement with another public school district, one of California’s leading districts. The district has also purchased robot devices including Master Mini and Aegis EDU. Third, we signed a Strategic Education Partnership Framework Agreement with an additional major public school district in Los Angeles.

The second and third partnerships both cover K–12 through adult education. We’ll work with the two districts to develop curricula together, set up innovation labs, create career and technical education pathways, train teachers, and give students hands-on experience. Together, we’ll explore how Physical AI education can connect what students learn in the classroom with further study, real-world practice, and career development. These two collaborations both renew automatically at the end of their terms. With these frameworks in place, we can move future projects forward quickly through a streamlined process.

Outside of California, we are also moving forward with strategic partnerships and sales in robotics education across multiple school districts in four other states: New York, Pennsylvania, Florida, and Texas. FFR pioneered K–12 robotics education in the U.S., and we’re now No. 1 in the industry. The progress we’ve made on strategic partnerships and robot purchases across these three leading districts matters to FFR and to the whole industry. Let me share four reasons why:

First, it’s a big step forward for our education ecosystem. By working with major school districts as strategic partners at the school district level, we can work directly with the U.S. public education system to build Physical AI education pathways that connect K–12 learning, technical skills training, and future careers.

Second, these projects give us a model for replicating at scale nationwide. The U.S. has more than 13,000 regular public-school districts. Across the country, about 130,000 public and private K–12 schools serve roughly 53 million students. That’s a large market, with opportunities across robot devices, curricula, teacher training, and ongoing services. We’ll learn from our first projects with leading districts, turn what works into a repeatable model, and gradually roll it out to across the country.

Third, it helps us move faster on our Four-Core Full-Stack AI business in education and speeds up the evolutionary flywheel. In real classrooms, we can deploy robot devices, develop Skills and solutions, and collect data in line with applicable requirements. That data helps us keep improving our Education Brain.

Fourth, it helps transform U.S. education in the Physical AI era. By making robots a regular part of teaching and hands-on learning, we can prepare the next generation of developers and skilled workers for the new era. As FFR’s profile in the industry grows, we’ve received invitations from schools, universities, and school districts to take part in academic discussions and major exhibitions. I’ll share more about those with you in future reports.

Regarding corporate governance, this week we welcomed Carolyn Kissane to FFR’s board as an independent director. Carolyn is the associate dean of New York University’s Center for Global Affairs. She brings years of experience in higher education and knows how to bring universities, researchers, and companies together. Carolyn could help us grow our robotics education ecosystem, reach more developers, and build more industry partnerships. She’ll also help us bring technology, talent, industry, and capital together. That will help us put our Four-Core Full-Stack AI strategy to work faster across all four industry ecosystems.

We also held our Middle East launch in Dubai this week. Six of our robots made their debut in the region. With our local partners, we showed five ways to put robots to work across our four industry ecosystems: education, security and inspection, entertainment, healthcare, and interactive sports. Together, we’re opening a new chapter for Physical AI in the Middle East. We’ll share a video from Dubai next week, so stay tuned.

For FFAI: it released its Q3 results this week. I want to highlight an important step we’ve taken on financial management and internal controls. After evaluating and testing the controls, FFAI management concluded that, as of September 30, 2026, FFAI had corrected all nine previously identified material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting. Management also concluded that the related controls were operating effectively. FFAI has spent nearly two years improving FFAI’s financial management and internal controls. This progress puts us in a stronger position to meet our obligations as a public company, raise capital, and rebuild trust with investors. It also gives us a stronger foundation to grow and create value through our shared Robotaxi network, AI VisiCabin operations, and Physical AI investment and holdings business. All right, thanks for tuning in. I’ll see you next week!”

Key Terms

material weaknessesfinancial
Material weaknesses are significant flaws in a company’s systems for ensuring its financial reports are accurate and reliable. Like a broken lock on a safe, they increase the chance that financial statements contain big errors or omissions, which can mislead investors about performance and risk; discovering one often raises questions about management oversight, may lead to restated results, and can affect investor confidence and a company’s valuation.
internal control over financial reportingfinancial
Internal control over financial reporting is a company’s system of procedures and checks designed to make sure its financial statements are accurate and complete, like a set of guardrails and verification steps that catch mistakes or fraud before numbers are published. Investors care because strong controls make reported results more trustworthy, lower the risk of surprise restatements or regulatory problems, and give greater confidence when valuing the company or comparing it to peers.

Opportunity to deliver an AI-led transformation of a major industrial business

MUMBAI, Nov. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Brookfield and Blackstone today announced that Brookfield, through its flagship private equity strategy, has agreed to acquire PGP Glass (“PGP”), a leading global specialty glass packaging manufacturer, from funds managed by Blackstone Private Equity.

PGP is a leading manufacturer of specialty glass packaging for cosmetics and perfumery, specialty food and beverage, and pharmaceutical industries, serving leading global brands in more than 70 countries. The company offers end-to-end solutions comprising design, mold-making, specialty glass manufacturing and decoration, supported by three manufacturing facilities across India and Sri Lanka, alongside an extensive global logistics and warehousing network.

Aditya Joshi, Managing Partner and Head of Private Equity for Brookfield in Asia Pacific and Middle East, said, “PGP is a high-quality manufacturer of specialty glass packaging, with a leadership position in premium categories and long-standing relationships with some of the world’s most recognizable brands. As demand for high-quality packaging continues to increase worldwide, Brookfield brings the scale and operating expertise to accelerate PGP’s growth through an AI-led transformation program.”

Amit Dalmia, Senior Managing Director and Head of the Blackstone Operating Team in Asia, said: “We are proud to have partnered with PGP Glass on its remarkable journey. Under the leadership of Vijay Shah, the management team has delivered outstanding operating performance, outpaced its peers and demonstrated leadership in sustainability. This investment embodies our ability to partner with exceptional management teams to build strong businesses that are built to last. We are pleased to welcome Brookfield as PGP’s next partner and wish the company continued success.”

Vijay Shah, Chief Executive Officer of PGP Glass, said: “We welcome Brookfield and look forward to working with them to accelerate our next phase of growth and value creation. Brookfield’s global footprint and substantial experience managing businesses across cycles will be particularly useful to us. We are grateful for Blackstone's partnership, which helped us expand capacity, strengthen our operations and sustainability leadership, and grow ahead of the industry.”

Investment Highlights

  • Market leader: PGP is a scaled, cost-advantaged manufacturer in the large premium glass packaging market, with a strong management team and a reputation for quality and customer service.
  • Attractive industry fundamentals: The glass packaging market benefits from established demand across a broad range of products and segments, with limited substitution risk in premium applications. Structural cost pressures and capacity rationalization among European and North American manufacturers create opportunities for efficient, high-quality producers such as PGP Glass to expand their market presence.
  • Growth strategy: Opportunity to accelerate growth through deeper penetration with existing customers, expansion into attractive markets, and targeted manufacturing capacity investments.
  • AI-led transformation: Opportunity to accelerate PGP’s AI-led transformation across the enterprise, including opportunities to enhance sales and operations planning, production efficiency and quality control.

Transaction Details

Brookfield’s investment will be funded through the Brookfield Capital Partners strategy and its affiliate Brookfield Business Corporation (NYSE: BBUC, TSX: BBUC).

The transaction remains subject to customary closing conditions including regulatory and government approvals. Closing is expected in Q1 2027.

The company offers high-quality, end-to-end specialty glass solutions including design, production, mould-making, decoration and packaging. With three state-of-the-art facilities in India and Sri Lanka, PGP Glass has 13 furnaces and production capacity of over 1,800 tonnes per day. It serves marquee global brands across over 70 countries through a global distribution and warehousing network, with overseas markets accounting for more than 70% of its sales. Four operational filter presses achieve a key filtration requirement toward commercial production

VANCOUVER, British Columbia, Nov. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Eldorado Gold Corporation (TSX: ELD, NYSE: EGO) (“Eldorado” or the “Company”) is pleased to announce that four tailings filter presses are now operational at its Skouries mine in northern Greece, marking another important milestone in the commissioning and ramp-up of the operation.

“With four filter presses now operational, we have achieved another important milestone in the ramp-up of Skouries,” said Christian Milau, President and Chief Executive Officer. “With this additional filtration capacity now online, we are well positioned to advance throughput and build momentum across the operation. We remain focused on progressing the ramp-up toward commercial production, which we expect late this quarter.”

Four operating filter presses are required to support commercial production on sulphide ore, with five required to achieve nameplate throughput. The Skouries tailings filtration facility comprises six Metso filter presses, including five operating units and one installed spare. The sixth unit provides operational flexibility and enables maintenance activities with no loss of throughput. The remaining two filter presses are expected to be operational in early December.

Technical Report

Eldorado expects to file an updated Technical Report for Skouries in the first quarter of 2027, incorporating an updated resource model and metal price assumptions, together with updated production, operating cost and capital estimates reflecting the transition of Skouries from development into operations.

Eldorado is a gold, copper and base metals producer with mining, development and exploration operations in Canada, Türkiye, and Greece. The Company has a highly skilled and dedicated workforce, safe and responsible operations, a portfolio of high-quality assets, and long-term partnerships with local communities. Eldorado’s common shares trade on the Toronto Stock Exchange (TSX: ELD) and the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE: EGO).

LONDON--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Smartphone shipments in Africa fell 40% year-on-year (YoY) to 13.7 million units, down from 22.8 million a year earlier, according to Omdia’s latest research. This marked the steepest YoY decline in three years following three consecutive years of third-quarter growth. Rising component costs and currency pressures are changing how vendors price their devices and how consumers buy them across Africa's largest markets.

Africa smartphone market shipment, 2Q23 to 3Q26

Rising prices weigh on smartphone shipments and market value

Shipments of smartphones priced below $100 fell nearly 70% YoY in 3Q26, while feature phone shipments grew 27%. Entry-level smartphones are becoming less profitable, prompting vendors to reconsider which models they offer and how they price them. Consumers who pay in cash, particularly those without access to operator subsidies or financing, are delaying upgrades or turning to refurbished smartphones and feature phones. Higher-priced smartphones are increasingly out of reach for these buyers.

“The figures show how affordability is shaping buying decisions in Africa. Some buyers are waiting longer to upgrade or choosing a refurbished smartphone to stay within budget,” notes Manish Pravinkumar, Principal Analyst at Omdia. “In many other regions, higher average selling prices (ASPs) helped sustain market value as shipments fell. In Africa, the ASP reached $222 in 3Q26, its highest third-quarter level in a decade. Even so, market value fell 15%. The increase in average price reflects a widening affordability gap and offers little evidence that buyers are moving to more expensive models.”

Nigeria and Egypt record the steepest shipment declines among Africa’s key markets

The size of the decline varied across Africa's key markets, reflecting differences in economic conditions, access to consumer financing, and exposure to currency and policy changes. Nigeria recorded the steepest decline among these markets, with smartphone shipments down 47% YoY. Fuel price pressures following subsidy removal, limited access to US dollars for import payments and higher handset costs further reduced household purchasing power.

In Egypt, smartphone shipments fell 41%. A weaker Egyptian pound and persistent inflation raised the cost of importing phones and manufacturing them locally, prompting consumers to delay upgrades.

In Kenya, smartphone shipments fell 35%. Shipments in the country’s core price segment, smartphones priced below $150, fell 44% as higher device prices put these devices beyond the reach of more buyers. Credit purchases and instalment plans are playing a growing role in helping consumers manage upfront costs.

South Africa recorded a smaller decline of 20%. Established operator distribution networks, contract upgrades, and a wider range of retail channels helped support shipments. High smartphone penetration, pressure on household budgets and longer replacement cycles continued to weigh on demand.

Samsung gains market share as TRANSSION retains the lead

TRANSSION accounted for 48% of smartphone shipments in Africa in 3Q26. Its shipments fell 43%, reflecting its exposure to the shrinking market for smartphones priced below $100.

Samsung recorded the smallest shipment decline among the five leading vendors, down 8%, and its market share rose to 23%. Its operator relationships and broad Galaxy A-series portfolio supported shipments. The Galaxy A07 4G and A17 4G together accounted for 56% of Samsung’s total smartphone shipments in Africa during the quarter.

Xiaomi’s shipments fell 49% as price increases across its portfolio weakened demand from channel partners and reduced its share of consumer spending.

HONOR’s shipments fell 14% YoY in 3Q26 after recording near triple-digit growth in the previous two years. Its performance in South Africa and expansion into other African markets supported that earlier growth. The decline shows how higher handset prices can slow even fast-growing vendors.

OPPO’s shipments fell 69% as it reorganized its operations as part of its integration with realme.

Tax reforms and device financing offer potential routes to recovery

Omdia expects smartphone shipments in Africa to end 2026 down 23% YoY and forecasts a further 25% decline in 2027.

“The forecast shows how heavily Africa's smartphone market depends on affordable devices and continued growth in shipments,” said Pravinkumar. “With cost pressures expected to persist into 2027, vendors face a difficult pricing challenge. They need to keep entry-level devices profitable, but passing higher component costs on to buyers risks putting smartphones beyond the reach of more households.”

Tax policy and access to financing will also shape the prospects for a recovery. Morocco reduced its smartphone import duty from 17.5% to 2.5%, illustrating how tax reform can ease cost pressures. Vodacom has introduced prepaid handset financing across all its African markets. In Nigeria, vivo is working with Credit Direct on device financing. M-KOPA continues to expand its smartphone financing model.

Pravinkumar added, “Governments, manufacturers and mobile operators all have a role in improving affordability. Closer cooperation will be essential to expand local manufacturing, make distribution more cost-effective, and give more customers access to financing. The next phase of growth depends on making connected devices affordable for a wider range of buyers.”

Key Terms

aspfinancial
Average selling price (ASP) is the typical price a company receives for a single unit of a product or service, calculated by dividing total revenue by units sold. Investors watch ASP because it shows whether a company is successfully charging more or less for its offerings — like checking the average price per loaf of bread a bakery sells — which directly affects revenue, profit margins, and the health of future sales.
sell-in shipmentstechnical
Sell-in shipments are the products a manufacturer or supplier sends to distributors, wholesalers or retailers during a reporting period; they count as sales to the channel but not yet as purchases by end customers. Investors watch sell-in because it shows how much stock is moving into the sales pipeline—like a factory delivering boxes to stores—which can signal future revenue growth but may overstate demand if retailers are simply building up inventory rather than selling to consumers.
import dutyregulatory
A charge imposed by a government on goods brought into a country, like a toll collected at a border crossing for imported products. It matters to investors because import duties raise the cost of goods, affect a company’s profit margin, pricing decisions and supply-chain choices, and can change consumer demand and competitive balance—factors that influence revenue, cash flow and the value of an investment.

Mr. Brett has been involved with the Company’s recently acquired Pasfield Lake Uranium Project in Saskatchewan’s Athabasca Basin for more than two decades. He will draw on that experience to advise the Company on reviewing historical exploration records and planning future exploration of the project.

Mr. Brett’s technical and exploration background Includes:

  • More than 30 years of international mineral exploration experience as a Senior Geophysical Consultant, in all geophysical methods and most commodities on five continents 

  • Consulting experience with more than 100 leading junior and major exploration and mining companies, as well as provincial and national governments, in Canada and internationally 

  • M.Sc. in Geology (Geophysics) and B.Sc. in Physics (Geophysics) from the University of Toronto 

  • Professional Geoscientist (P.Geo.) registered with Professional Geoscientists Ontario 

  • Extensive experience consulting to and directing geophysical and geological exploration programs 

  • Uranium experience in Athabasca-type and other uranium settings in Canada and internationally 

  • Served on the board of directors of the Prospectors and Developers Association of Canada (PDAC) 

  • Expertise in integrating geophysical, geological and physical-properties data with ore deposit models and structural geology to identify and test exploration targets 

David Greenway, Chief Executive Officer of Uranium One, commented: “Jeremy’s appointment brings valuable technical expertise and more than two decades of familiarity with Pasfield Lake to Uranium One. His experience integrating geophysical and geological data will help guide our evaluation of the project’s extensive historical exploration database and refine priorities for future exploration. As we advance our Athabasca Basin portfolio, we are focused on building the technical foundation needed to identify and systematically test compelling uranium targets.”

Biography

Mr. Brett is a Senior Geophysical Consultant who has designed, supervised, quality-assured and interpreted exploration programs for uranium, copper and a broad range of other commodities in North, Central and South America, Africa, Asia, Europe and the Middle East. He has advised more than 100 junior and major exploration and mining companies, as well as provincial and national governments. He has also served as the geophysics champion for the PDAC Exploration Assessment Digital Data Formats working group. His experience includes exploration program design, project management, data integration, target prioritization and target testing. He is familiar with the reporting requirements under National Instrument 43-101.

Mr. Brett specializes in integrating geophysical, geological and physical-properties data with ore deposit models and structural geology to identify and test exploration targets. He is a Professional Geoscientist (P.Geo.) registered with Professional Geoscientists Ontario. He is a Fellow of the Society of Economic Geologists (SEG) and a member of the Canadian Exploration Geophysical Society (KEGS), Professional Engineers & Geoscientists Newfoundland & Labrador (PEGNL), and the Prospectors and Developers Association of Canada (PDAC).

Pasfield Lake Project, Athabasca Basin

The Pasfield Lake Project is Uranium One’s flagship Canadian uranium exploration asset, encompassing approximately 4,400 hectares in Saskatchewan’s eastern Athabasca Basin. Strategically located approximately 60 kilometres northwest of Cameco’s Cigar Lake Mine, the project occupies a highly prospective geological setting where favourable basement rocks, major regional fault systems, and historical exploration results combine to create an exceptional exploration opportunity.

Historical work completed by previous operators has generated an extensive technical database, including airborne geophysical surveys, Audio Magnetotelluric (AMT) surveys, gravity surveys, geochemistry, and diamond drilling. This comprehensive dataset provides Uranium One with a strong foundation to apply modern exploration techniques and advanced targeting methods in the search for a significant uranium discovery.

NORWICH, England--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Cadeler has published its Q3 2026 Earnings Release, reflecting continued strong performance, with revenue for the third quarter up by 65% compared to the same period in 2025. The quarter saw further expansion of the fleet and of the company’s capabilities: In July, Cadeler took delivery of its second A-class vessel, Wind Ace, and in August it acquired Menck, strengthening its full-scope foundation installation offering.

Revenue for the first nine months of 2026 reached EUR 663 million, up 94% from EUR 342 million for the same period last year, while EBITDA was EUR 321 million, up 52% from EBITDA of EUR 211 million in 2025 (in each case, when adjusting for one-off termination fees of EUR 111 million in the comparative period).

Profit for the first nine months of 2026 was EUR 143 million, up 18% from EUR 121 million in the comparative period, when adjusting for the termination fees identified above.

Utilisation of Cadeler’s 11 vessels was 69.8%, compared with 75.8% across eight operating vessels over the same period last year, while contracted days increased by 44%, reflecting increased activity across the enlarged fleet.

Cadeler maintains its full-year 2026 guidance, with full-year revenue expected to be within the range of EUR 910 million to 1,000 million, which includes an anticipated hammer sale scheduled to complete in December 2026. Full-year EBITDA is expected to be within the range of EUR 435 million to 525 million, when excluding costs related to the acquisition and integration of Menck.

Mikkel Gleerup, CEO of Cadeler, comments:

“These results demonstrate that our strategy is translating into strong execution and continued growth. During the period, we have delivered solid operational and financial performance, welcomed Wind Ace to our fleet and, through the acquisition of Menck, significantly strengthened the capabilities we can offer within full-scope foundation transport and installation. Together, these developments give us greater flexibility to respond to changing project requirements and support our customers with the reliability, resilience and certainty of delivery they increasingly require. With a strong backlog and continued demand for our vessels and services, we remain focused on disciplined execution across our projects while building the capabilities required for the next phase of offshore wind development.”

Acquisition of Menck

Cadeler completed the acquisition of Menck in August 2026 for an enterprise value of EUR 501 million. The acquisition combines Menck’s specialist equipment and engineering expertise with Cadeler’s installation fleet and experience, enabling a more integrated foundation installation offering for the group’s customers. Menck continues to operate as a standalone business, preserving its independent market position. The transaction was financed through available liquidity and a EUR 380 million acquisition facility. Menck contributed approximately EUR 24.1 million of revenue and EUR 1.1 million of net profit from 11 August to 30 September 2026.

Backlog and commercial momentum

As of 23 November 2026, Cadeler’s contract backlog, including options, stands at EUR 2.4 billion.

The backlog includes a firm contract, signed after the reporting period, to support the transportation and installation of wind turbines at Dogger Bank C in the UK, the third 1.2GW phase of the world’s largest offshore wind farm under construction and the operational debut for Wind Apex.

Cadeler also announced the signing of a significant exclusivity agreement (not included in the group’s contract backlog) with an undisclosed client for wind turbine and foundation installation at a large-scale offshore wind farm in the UK. That installation campaign is expected to commence in 2030, with the foundations campaign to be executed using an A-class vessel and an O-class vessel, and the wind turbines to be installed by a P-class vessel.

Fleet expansion and newbuild programme

By mid-2027, Cadeler expects to operate a 12-vessel fleet, the largest and most versatile in the offshore wind industry.

Wind Ace joined the fleet in July 2026 on schedule and within budget. Designed for both foundation and turbine installation, its first project will be ScottishPower Renewables’ East Anglia TWO, where offshore installation is planned to begin in 2027. The construction of Cadeler’s third A-class vessel, Wind Apex, is similarly progressing on schedule.

In August, Cadeler signed firm contracts with COSCO Shipping Offshore for two T-class vessels, due for delivery in 2030 and 2031. Incorporating breakthrough technologies, the T-class vessels will be the largest and most capable vessels in the offshore installation and foundation market.

Redomiciliation to the United Kingdom

Cadeler successfully completed its redomiciliation to the United Kingdom on 4 November 2026, following acceptance of the voluntary share exchange offer by holders representing 92.06% of Cadeler A/S shares. Cadeler plc’s shares began trading on the Oslo and New York stock exchanges on 5 November 2026. Cadeler plc intends to acquire the remaining 7.94% of Cadeler A/S shares for approximately EUR 173 million. The establishment of a UK-incorporated parent company positions the Group to attract a broader and more diverse international investor base, while creating a corporate structure that better reflects the scale and global reach of Cadeler’s activities. The redomiciliation will have no impact on Cadeler’s personnel, geographic footprint or project operations.

Strong balance sheet and strategic financing initiatives

As of 30 September 2026, Cadeler’s total assets stood at EUR 4.5 billion, up 31+% year-to-date. This includes a EUR 484 million increase in property, plant and equipment, primarily attributable to newbuilds and various vessel upgrades, as well as the acquisition of Menck. Total equity increased to EUR 1.9 billion as of 30 September 2026, reflecting an increase of EUR 347 million from the balance at year end 2025 of EUR 1.5 billion.

In July 2026, Cadeler announced the signing of an EIFO-backed green term loan facility of EUR 247 million to fund the delivery of Wind Apex, expected in Q2 2027.

Earnings Call

In connection with the publication of its Q3 2026 Earnings Release, Cadeler will host a live video webcast presentation for the investment community. Mikkel Gleerup, Chief Executive Officer, and Peter Brogaard Hansen, Chief Financial Officer, will present live from London.

Date: 23 November 2026
Time: 08:00 EST / 13:00 UK / 14:00 CET

The earnings presentation is open to all interested parties and may include forward-looking information. Please register in advance at this link https://cadeler-q3-2026-earnings-presentation.open-exchange.net/registration.

A replay of the webcast and the presentation slides will be made available on Cadeler’s Investor Relations website following the presentation, available here: http://www.cadeler.com/investor.

Cadeler plc (Cadeler) is a global leader in offshore wind turbine transport and installation. The company owns and operates the industry’s largest fleet of jack-up offshore wind installation vessels and is expanding its capabilities into full-scope foundation transport and installation, as well as operations & maintenance. NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Morgan Stanley Investment Management (MSIM), through investment funds managed by Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners (MSIP), its private infrastructure investment platform, today announced it has entered into an agreement to sell StraitNZ (the Company), a New Zealand-based integrated transport, logistics and ferry company, to Partners Group, a leading global private markets firm, acting on behalf of its clients.

StraitNZ manages multiple daily freight and passenger services across the Cook Strait in New Zealand. StraitNZ is one of only two Cook Strait ferry operators, connecting New Zealand’s national highway system from the North Island to the South Island. Since MSIP’s investment in March 2022, the Company completed a full fleet refresh, introduced three-year CPI-linked take-or-pay freight contracts, rolled out dynamic passenger pricing, secured multi-decade port lease extensions and delivered strong EBITDA growth.

“StraitNZ demonstrates MSIP’s ability to identify high-quality essential infrastructure businesses and create value through active ownership and disciplined execution,” said Mark McLean, Managing Director and Co-Head of Asia-Pacific investing for MSIP. “Over our ownership period, we have worked alongside management to strengthen the Company’s commercial proposition, improve operational performance and position StraitNZ for sustainable long-term growth.”

Through its ferries and nationwide road freight network, StraitNZ provides an essential freight and passenger link, connecting customers, communities and businesses across New Zealand’s supply chain. Services are expected to continue as normal while the transaction is completed.

The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to customary regulatory approvals and other closing conditions.

MILPITAS, Calif., Nov. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Zepp Health Corporation (NYSE: ZEPP) ("Zepp", the "Company" or "we") today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter of 2026.

Third Quarter of 2026 Financial and Operating Highlights:

  • Revenue reached US$68.3 million, representing a year-over-year decrease of 9.9% and a quarter-over-quarter increase of 7.5%.
  • Gross margin was 35.0%, compared with 38.2% and 37.4% in the same period of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026, respectively. Gross margin faced several headwinds during the quarter, primarily elevated memory and other component costs, as well as foreign currency impacts. While product mix improved year-over-year, this favorable mix benefit was more than offset by higher memory costs within our entry-level price segments.
  • GAAP and adjusted net loss[1] attributable to Zepp were US$12.6 million and US$11.6 million, respectively, compared with US$1.6 million and US$0.7 million in the same period of 2025, and US$11.3 million and US$12.5 million in the second quarter of 2026. The net loss was due to lower gross margin mainly resulting from higher memory and other component costs and foreign currency headwinds, as well as increased investment in marketing and branding activities.
  • As of September 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents and restricted cash totaled US$99.0 million, compared with US$102.6 million as of September 30, 2025 and US$106.3 million as of June 30, 2026.
  • Product Innovation: Launched T-Rex Dual Solar, pairing a bright AMOLED display with solar charging through both the front of the watch and its glass-ceramic back. It offers up to 25 days of battery life under typical use, and its dual-sided solar charging and offline navigation are designed for multi-day trips outdoors.
  • Software Ecosystem: Rolled out Zepp OS 6 to more existing watch models and made HYROX post-race station analysis available on more models. These updates give customers more value from the devices they already own and help build confidence in Amazfit's ongoing support for its products.

[1] Adjusted net income/(loss) attributable to Zepp Health Corporation represents net income/(loss) excluding (i) share-based compensation expenses, (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from acquisitions and business cooperation agreements, (iii) gain/(loss) from fair value change of long-term investments, (iv) impairment loss from long-term investments, (v) income/(loss) from equity method investments, (vi) investment income/(loss) and (vii) tax effects of the above non-GAAP adjustments. See "Reconciliation of GAAP and Non-GAAP Results" at the end of this press release.

"The third quarter was a period of adjustment for us," said Wayne Huang, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Zepp Health. "Tight supply for some of our core products weighed on revenue, while unfavorable exchange rates and higher prices for memory and other chips put pressure on gross margin. The adjustments we made across our products, training software, supply, and retail are already beginning to pay off in the fourth quarter, and we are heading into the holiday season and the year ahead with momentum.

In the third quarter, global activations across the Balance family rose approximately 40% from the second quarter, driven by our new, higher-priced models. Combined global activations for Active 3 Premium and Active Max, our two US$169 models, grew approximately 35% over the same period. We also expanded our premium outdoor lineup with T-Rex Dual Solar, a watch priced at about US$650 that pairs a bright AMOLED display with dual-sided solar charging and offline navigation for multi-day trips. Through Zepp OS 6 and HYROX updates, we brought new training tools to more watches that customers already own, giving them more value from their devices.

Product availability has started to improve in some markets in the fourth quarter, including for T-Rex 3. We have also made it easier for customers to compare watches in stores. At REI, we provided materials to help shoppers compare models. Large screens are now in place at our Amazfit counters in select Best Buy stores. They make the counters easier to spot and show shoppers how our devices fit into everyday activity, training, and recovery. As more products reach store shelves, we believe we will be better positioned to meet holiday demand."

Leon Deng, Chief Financial Officer of Zepp Health, commented, "Third-quarter revenue reached US$68.3 million, up 7.5% sequentially and within our guidance range. While revenue declined 9.9% year-over-year, we continued to see encouraging momentum in our Active series. Supply constraints on certain higher-margin products, including Balance 3 and Helio Strap, limited our ability to fully capture market demand during the quarter.

Gross margin was 35.0%, compared with 37.4% in the previous quarter and 38.2% in the same period last year, reflecting unfavorable foreign exchange movements, continued increases in memory component costs, and supply constraints on our higher-margin products. Importantly, excluding the tariff-related benefit recorded in the second quarter, our underlying gross margin remained strong sequentially. Continued improvement in our product mix helped offset a meaningful portion of these external cost pressures, demonstrating the progress we have made in strengthening our premium product portfolio and underlying unit economics.

We continued to balance financial discipline with targeted investments to support future growth. On a sequential basis, adjusted operating expenses decreased to US$34.2 million, and adjusted operating loss narrowed to US$10.3 million. The year-over-year increase in operating expenses was primarily driven by strategic investments in new product launches, brand building, athlete partnerships, and distribution expansion. At the same time, general and administrative expenses declined, reflecting our ongoing efforts to improve operational efficiency and manage our structural cost base.

We ended the quarter with US$99.0 million in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash, while inventory declined to US$68.6 million from US$87.7 million a year earlier. We also continued to strengthen our balance sheet by extending our debt maturity profile, converting an additional US$26.6 million of short-term borrowings into longer-term obligations during the quarter. We remain committed to returning value to shareholders through our ongoing share repurchase program. As of September 30, 2026, we had cumulatively repurchased US$17.8 million under our US$20 million authorization, and our board of directors recently approved a one-year extension of the existing program.

Looking ahead, we expect fourth-quarter revenue to be between US$90.0 million and US$95.0 million, representing year-over-year growth of approximately 6% to 12%. As product availability improves and our expanded distribution channels begin contributing more meaningfully, we remain focused on translating our investments into stronger revenue growth and greater operating leverage. Despite near-term external cost pressures, we believe our improving product mix, disciplined cost management, and continued investment in the Amazfit brand are building a stronger foundation for sustainable long-term growth and profitability."

Third Quarter of 2026 Financial Results

Revenues

Revenue reached US$68.3 million, representing a year-over-year decrease of 9.9% and a quarter-over-quarter increase of 7.5%. The year-over-year decline was due to the broader macroeconomic environment and a strong comparison base, as well as supply constraints on top-selling offerings, particularly Helio Strap and Balance 3. However, revenue from the Active series increased significantly year-over-year.

Gross Margin

Gross margin was 35.0%, compared with 38.2% and 37.4% in the same period of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026, respectively. Gross margin faced several headwinds during the quarter, primarily elevated memory and other component costs, as well as foreign currency impacts. While product mix improved year-over-year, supported by new product introductions including the Active series, this favorable mix benefit was more than offset by higher memory costs within our entry-level price segments. Gross margin for the second quarter of 2026 benefited from tariff refunds that the Company recorded related to duties previously remitted under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act ("IEEPA"). Excluding the impact of these refunds, gross margin increased sequentially.

Research and Development Expenses

Research and development expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were US$11.4 million, compared with US$10.8 million and US$11.5 million in the third quarter of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026, respectively. Excluding US$0.6 million of foreign currency headwinds, research and development expenses were flat compared with the same period of 2025. We continued to invest in a series of cutting-edge products as well as new technologies, including AI, to maintain our competitive edge against our peers. At the same time, we focused on refined research and development approaches, consistently evaluating resource efficiency to optimize return on investment and productivity.

Selling and Marketing Expenses

Selling and marketing expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were US$18.0 million, compared with US$12.0 million and US$18.3 million in the third quarter of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026, respectively. The US$6.0 million year-over-year increase was primarily attributable to US$1.9 million investment across online and offline channels for content refreshes, in-store displays and holiday season readiness, and US$1.5 million of launch campaigns for new products including the Balance 3, Balance Ultra and T-Rex Dual Solar. The remainder of the increase reflected US$1.4 million for marathons, Ultra-Trail du Mont-Blanc (UTMB) and media sponsorships, and US$1.2 million related to the HYROX and new athletes partnerships.

General and Administrative Expenses

General and administrative expenses were US$5.6 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with US$7.0 million and US$6.2 million in the third quarter of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026, respectively. We continued to streamline overhead, maintaining disciplined cost control while improving operating efficiency.

Operating Expenses

GAAP and adjusted operating expenses[2] for the third quarter of 2026 were US$35.0 million and US$34.2 million, respectively, compared with US$29.8 million and US$28.6 million in the third quarter of 2025, and US$36.0 million and US$34.8 million in the second quarter of 2026. Out of the year-over-year increase of US$5.2 million in operating expenses, US$0.8 million was due to foreign currency impacts. The remaining US$4.4 million was primarily due to higher selling and marketing expenses as mentioned above. On a quarter-over-quarter basis, operating expenses decreased slightly.

Operating Income/(Loss)

GAAP and adjusted operating results[3] were loss of US$11.1 million and loss of US$10.3 million, respectively, compared with loss of US$0.9 million and income of US$0.4 million in the same quarter of 2025. The net operating loss was due to lower gross margin mainly resulting from higher memory and other component costs and foreign currency headwinds, as well as increased investment in marketing and branding activities, but the operating loss narrowed compared with the second quarter of 2026. 

Net Income/(Loss)

GAAP and adjusted net loss attributable to Zepp for the third quarter of 2026 were US$12.6 million and US$11.6 million, respectively, compared with GAAP and adjusted net loss of US$1.6 million and US$0.7 million for the same quarter in 2025. The US$10.9 million year-over-year increase in adjusted net loss was primarily driven by a US$6.0 million increase in selling and marketing expenses, as discussed above, followed by a US$3.2 million unfavorable foreign exchange impact. In addition, higher memory and other component costs resulted in a net US$2.7 million gross profit headwind, partially mitigated by a more favorable product mix. These unfavorable impacts were partially offset by US$1.1 million in savings from general and administrative expenses.

[2] Adjusted operating expenses represent operating expenses excluding (i) share-based compensation expenses and (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from acquisitions and business cooperation agreements. Please refer to the section titled "Reconciliation of GAAP and Non-GAAP Results" at the end of this press release.

[3] Adjusted operating income/(loss) represents operating income/(loss) excluding: (i) share-based compensation expenses and (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from acquisitions and business cooperation agreements. See "Reconciliation of GAAP and Non-GAAP Results" at the end of this press release.

Liquidity and Capital Resources

As of September 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents and restricted cash were US$99.0 million, compared with US$102.6 million and US$106.3 million as of September 30, 2025 and June 30, 2026, respectively.

The Company recorded inventory of US$68.6 million as of September 30, 2026, compared with US$62.4 million as of June 30, 2026 and US$87.7 million as of September 30, 2025. We will continue to manage the inventory level tightly and working capital closely.

Long-term and short-term debt levels remained flat as of September 30, 2026 compared with June 30, 2026. We remain committed to prudently managing our debt profile. Our primary objective is to maintain overall debt levels broadly stable while actively extending the maturity profile by replacing short-term borrowings with long-term debt. During the third quarter and for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, we successfully converted US$26.6 million and US$56.5 million, respectively, of short-term debt into long-term obligations, and we expect to continue this strategy in the coming quarters, supported by sufficient financial headroom and liquidity capacity. Since the beginning of 2023, the Company has cumulatively retired US$38.1 million of debt, and will continue to optimize its capital structure.

Share Repurchase Program Update

The Company announced in its third quarter 2021 earnings release that the board had authorized a share repurchase program of up to US$20 million through November 2022. On November 21, 2022, the board authorized a 12-month extension of the Company's share repurchase program. On November 20, 2023, the board further authorized the Company to extend its share repurchase program for another 12 months. On November 18, 2024, the board further authorized the Company to extend its share repurchase program for another 24 months. On November 22, 2026, the board further authorized the Company to extend its share repurchase program for another 12 months. Pursuant to the extended share repurchase program, the Company may repurchase its shares in the form of ADSs and/or ordinary shares through November 2027 with an aggregate value equal to the remaining balance under the share repurchase program. As of September 30, 2026, the Company had used US$17.8 million to repurchase approximately 2.4 million ADSs. The Company expects to fund the repurchases under the extended share repurchase program out of its existing cash balance.

Outlook

For the fourth quarter of 2026, the Company's management currently expects net revenues to be between US$90.0 million and US$95.0 million, which would represent an increase by approximately 6% to 12% from US$85.2 million in the fourth quarter of 2025.

This outlook is based on current market conditions and reflects the Company's current and preliminary estimates of market, operating conditions and customer demand, which are all subject to change.

  • As the first Chinese automaker to introduce public advanced ADAS test rides at a European retail store, XPENG brings intelligent driving beyond industry showcases and closer to everyday consumers, joining Tesla as only one of two global automakers bringing advanced ADAS experiences to European consumers.
  • The initiative marks XPENG's first overseas retail-based intelligent driving test ride experience, building on its large-scale public debut at the 2026 Paris Motor Show.
  • Powered by XPENG's VLA 2.0 architecture, NGP is undergoing European testing and localisation ahead of its planned international rollout in 2027, subject to regulatory approval and market readiness.

PARIS, Nov. 22, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- XPENG (NYSE: XPEV, HKEX: 9868), a leading Physical AI company, today announced the launch of public advanced ADAS test rides at its Paris store, marking its first overseas retail-based intelligent driving experience. The initiative makes XPENG the first Chinese automaker to offer public urban advanced ADAS test rides through a European retail location, bringing the technology closer to European consumers on real city roads.


Powered by XPENG's VLA 2.0 architecture, Next Generation Pilot (NGP) is an AI-powered advanced driver-assistance system designed to support drivers in complex, real-world driving scenarios. At the 2026 Paris Motor Show, XPENG and Tesla were the only two automakers globally to participate in the event's official Autonomous Lab programme, offering visitors the opportunity to experience advanced intelligent driving technology on real Paris roads. The Paris store initiative builds on this milestone, extending the experience beyond the motor show and bringing the technology closer to European consumers.

At XPENG's store at 10 boulevard Gouvion-Saint-Cyr in Paris, customers can book advanced ADAS test rides to experience NGP on real city roads, including dense urban traffic, complex intersections and other challenging driving environments. The experience gives European consumers a firsthand look at the capabilities of advanced intelligent driving in real-world conditions.


The Paris initiative comes as XPENG continues to test and localise its advanced driver-assistance technology for European road conditions and regulatory requirements, ahead of its planned international rollout in 2027, subject to regulatory approvals and market readiness.

He Xiaopeng, Chairman & CEO of XPENG, said: “Our mission is to bring Physical AI into everyday life and make advanced intelligent driving accessible to users worldwide. At the Paris Motor Show, many people asked when they could experience our technology themselves. Today, we are taking that next step.

For us, this is not just about showcasing technology, but about understanding how people experience it in the real world. Backed by our full-stack R&D and continuous localisation efforts, we are committed to listening to European customers, adapting our technology to their needs, and working towards safer, smarter and more seamless mobility experiences. This is what ‘In Europe, For Europe, With Europe’ means to us.”


Romain Caubet, Country Manager of XPENG in France, said, “At the Paris Motor Show, we introduced European audiences to our advanced driving assistance technology through real-world demonstrations. Today, we are bringing that experience closer to customers through our Paris store. Paris offers a unique and challenging urban driving environment, making it an ideal location for people to experience the technology firsthand. We look forward to hearing their feedback as we continue to develop our intelligent driving experience for European customers.”

XPENG is also contributing to international discussions on automated driving through its role as OICA Secretary for the United Nations Economic Commission for Europe (UNECE) TF-ESRI taskforce.

About XPENG

XPENG is a leading global Physical AI company, dedicated to bringing artificial intelligence into the physical world to reshape future mobility and smart living. Through in-house R&D, XPENG has developed a full-stack Physical AI architecture spanning Turing AI chips, world foundation models, and highly integrated software and hardware applications. This unified technology foundation of XPENG powers an expansive product portfolio of smart EVs, robotaxis, and humanoid robots, advancing the deployment of Physical AI at scale.

Headquartered in Guangzhou, China, XPENG is dual-primary listed on the New York Stock Exchange and the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. With global capabilities across R&D, manufacturing, sales, and services, XPENG drives continuous technological innovation and fosters an open Physical AI ecosystem, making life smarter, safer, and better for users worldwide. HOUSTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)--ConocoPhillips (NYSE: COP) today announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to sell its Norway business and its 40.25% interest in and operatorship of the U.K. Teesside oil terminal to Vår Energi for total consideration of $4.425 billion, less agreed upon adjustments of approximately $0.5 billion as of the Jan. 1, 2026, effective date. The transaction is expected to close by the end of the first quarter 2027 subject to approval by the Norwegian Ministry of Energy and regulatory conditions.

At closing, Vår Energi will assume the post-effective date balance sheets of the properties. Total consideration is expected to be $3.9 billion, including the remaining 2026 tax liability of approximately $1.4 billion, payable in the first half of 2027, and net cash proceeds of approximately $2.5 billion. Proceeds will be earmarked for general purposes and for discretionary share repurchases in 2027 to supplement the company’s long-standing commitment of returning approximately 45% of cash from operations to shareholders.

“We are extremely proud of the legacy we created with these assets for more than five decades and are pleased that Vår Energi recognizes the value of this business,” said Andy O’Brien, president and chief executive officer. “Norway and Teesside are high-quality assets with strong operating histories, and we believe this win-win transaction unlocks value for ConocoPhillips while positioning these assets for continued success under new ownership.”

The transaction includes the entire issued share capital of ConocoPhillips Skandinavia AS and ConocoPhillips (U.K.) Teesside Operator Limited, which together hold the company's Norway and Teesside assets and associated decommissioning liabilities.

The Norway business includes ConocoPhillips' interests in producing assets on the Norwegian continental shelf, anchored by the operated Greater Ekofisk Area in the North Sea, as well as interests in eight partner-operated fields across the Norwegian Sea and northern North Sea. It also includes the company's interest in the Norpipe oil pipeline and certain non-operated infrastructure. The Teesside business includes the Teesside oil terminal and related pipeline infrastructure.

In 2025, the Norway business produced approximately 120 thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day. Year-end 2025 proved reserves associated with the sale properties were approximately 221 million barrels of oil equivalent.

ConocoPhillips is a global exploration and production company with a deep, durable and diverse portfolio of oil and natural gas assets and a compelling pipeline of organic growth opportunities. Our disciplined, returns-focused strategy is designed to create long-term value and position ConocoPhillips to thrive across a range of market conditions. Learn more at www.conocophillips.com.
